svg.title: The excavation record, filled twice for one case
svg.desc: LIA's proposed minimal record format filled for Swanson's fish-oil and Raynaud's hypothesis as of 1986 and as of 1989, with the nine changed fields marked, the six suggested statuses, and novelty and validity drawn as separate axes.
svg.text: EDGELESS LAB / LATENT INFORMATION ARCHAEOLOGY / PLATE IV-04-1
One finding written twice: the fish-oil record as of 1986 and as of 1989
The record has 15 top-level fields, and each entry under sources carries three of its own. When the 1989 trial arrives, nine fields change; sources and limitations gain
entries, and the other six stand as they were.
AS OF 1989: AFTER THE FIRST REPORTED TRIAL
Dietary fish oil might benefit patients with Raynaud's syndrome.
Dietary fish oil improves tolerance to cold and delays the onset of vasospasm in patients with
Two sets of published medical articles: one on dietary fish oil, one on Raynaud's
Two entries, each from Swanson's 1989 summary: fish oil leads to blood and
vascular changes; similar changes might benefit Raynaud patients. available_at:
Adds DiGiacomo, Kremer and Shah (1989): 32 patients randomized to fish oil or olive-oil
placebo; median time to onset rose from 31.3 to 46.5 minutes at six weeks (p = 0.04).
If fish oil produces these changes, and these changes might benefit Raynaud
patients, then fish oil might benefit Raynaud patients.
The trial abstract gives its own rationale, a favorable vascular response to ischemia; the benefit
does not confirm each link of the 1986 inference.
No benefit concluded for patients with secondary Raynaud's syndrome.
Scope: the two sets of articles. Method: shared articles, joint citation, mention.
Result: no articles in common; never cited together; neither set mentioned the
One double-blind, placebo-controlled trial: among primary patients, an episode could no
longer be induced in 5 of 11 on fish oil against 1 of 9 on olive oil (p = 0.05).
Both evidence lines come from Swanson's own summary; publication years of the
Adds: one trial, one regimen, 32 patients; the trial is held as an abstract only.
A controlled clinical trial of dietary fish oil in patients with Raynaud's syndrome.
A second, independent trial in the primary form. None is recorded in the sources used here.
LIA lists them without thresholds, so the validation field carries the reason for the choice.
thalidomide in ENL, if recovered today
“Each of these is a pair of answers, one about novelty and one about validity.” One status word
cannot hold both, so the format keeps the first in novelty_check and the second in validation.
Novelty and validity are separate axes
A rediscovery can be true, and a novel candidate can be false.
new relative to a defined record
Scope sits inside novelty_check: the Antikythera mechanism was recovered in 1901, and the 2006 reconstruction
is new where the earlier recognition of an astronomical mechanism is not. The 105 years run to the
Sources: Swanson 1989, Bulletin of the Medical Library Association; DiGiacomo, Kremer and Shah 1989 (abstract); ledger rows RB-016, RB-014, RB-027, RB-019; LIA
long-form, Chapter IV-04. Field names are the LIA v0.1 template's own.
